question: When 23 online symptom checkers were tested on standard patient cases, how often did they name the right diagnosis first?
answer: About a third of the time. A 2015 Harvard audit fed them 45 written cases; the correct diagnosis came first in 34% and in the top 20 in 58%. Triage advice leaned cautious, sending people to doctors for problems safe to treat at home. A list of twenty guesses reads like an answer.
move: A long list of possibilities is not a diagnosis.
reference: Semigran, Linder, Gidengil & Mehrotra, Evaluation of symptom checkers for self diagnosis and triage: audit study, BMJ, 2015
